items.stem: 다음 중 밑줄 친 어휘의 쓰임이 문맥상 적절하지 <u>않은</u> 것은?
choices: The detective found a <u>clue</u> near the door.
She <u>wrapped</u> the gift in colorful paper.
The box was <u>empty</u>, so there was nothing inside.
Emily was moved by the <u>ordinary</u> life story of the hero.
Model airplanes were <u>hanging</u> from the ceiling.
items.explain: 영웅의 '위대한(great)' 삶의 이야기에 감동받았다는 흐름. ordinary(평범한)는 어색하다.

items.stem: 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 단어로 적절한 것은?
items.box:
• The old newspaper _____, "Women couldn't enter flight schools."
• I _____ a detective novel in the living room yesterday.
items.explain: read: (신문 등에) ~라고 쓰여 있다 / (책을) 읽다. 과거형 read.

items.stem: 우리말을 영어로 옮긴 것으로 적절하지 <u>않은</u> 것은?
choices:
그녀는 놀라서 방을 둘러보았다.
⇒ She looked around the room in surprise.

나는 요즘 살을 빼려고 노력하고 있다.
⇒ I'm trying to lose weight these days.

그는 한국의 독립을 위해 싸웠다.
⇒ He fought for Korea's independence.

그녀는 포기하지 않았다.
⇒ She didn't give in.

나는 그를 빨리 만나고 싶다.
⇒ I can't wait to meet him.
items.explain: 포기하다 = give up. give in 은 '굴복하다'.

items.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
items.explain: be interested in ~: ~에 관심이 있다.

items.box:
Junho: I can't find my new smartphone. Can you help me?
Kate: I'm sorry to hear that. I'll call you.
Junho: Actually, I turned it off.
Alex: ____ⓐ____
Junho: It's black, and there's a brown bear character on the cover.
Alex: When did you use it last?
Junho: I turned it off before class. Then I think I put it in my backpack.
Kate: Let's look around the classroom.
(a few minutes later)
Kate: I found it! It was inside your textbook.
Junho: Oh, thank you for helping me!

items.stem: 위 대화의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은? (문장의 의미와 어법 모두 고려할 것)
items.explain: 생김새를 묻는 표현 What does it look like? (How does it look? 은 like 없이 쓴다.)

items.stem: 위 대화를 읽고 답변할 수 <u>없는</u> 내용의 질문은?
choices: When did Junho use his smartphone last?
Why did Junho turn off his smartphone?
items.explain: 전원을 끈 이유는 대화에 나오지 않는다. (검은색 / 수업 전 / 교과서 안 / Kate)

items.box:
B: Yumi, what are you doing?
G: I'm reading a book about Neil Armstrong. I'm interested in his journey to the moon.
B: That sounds ____ⓐ____!
G: My dream is to become an astronaut like him.
B: I hope your dream comes true.
B:Boy / G:Girl

items.stem: 위 대화의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
items.explain: That sounds + 형용사. 감정을 일으키는 대상이므로 amazing.

items.stem: 위 대화의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 유미는 Neil Armstrong에 관한 영상을 보고 있다.
유미는 Neil Armstrong의 달 여행에 관심이 있다.
items.explain: I'm interested in his journey to the moon.

items.stem: 자연스러운 대화가 되도록 (A)~(D)를 바르게 배열한 것은?
items.box:
B: Oh! I lost my backpack!
(A) G: What does it look like?
(B) B: Hmm.... I think I left it on the basketball court.
(C) G: I'm sorry to hear that. Where did you last see it?
(D) B: It's a blue backpack with a star pattern on it.
G: Oh, let's go to the basketball court and look for it.
items.explain: 유감 표현·마지막으로 본 곳 질문(C) → 농구 코트(B) → 생김새 질문(A) → 별무늬 파란 배낭(D).

items.box:
Junho: Minji, what are you reading?
Minji: I'm reading this book My Life with the Chimpanzees.
Junho: Are you interested in chimpanzees?
Minji: Yes, I am. This book is about the life of Jane Goodall and her love for chimpanzees.
Alex: I read the book, too. She's an animal scientist who studied chimpanzees for many years.
Minji: You're right. She's the first person to study chimpanzees in the wild. ⓐ<u>She's my role model.</u>
Junho: Wow, that's great!
Minji: Like Jane Goodall, I'm very interested in animal behavior. And I want to study animals in the wild and help them, too.
Alex: I hope your dream comes true.

items.stem: 위 대화의 내용으로 볼 때 민지가 앞으로 할 가능성이 가장 높은 활동은?
choices: Marie Curie에 관한 과학 프로젝트 하기
items.explain: I want to study animals in the wild and help them, too.

items.stem: 위 대화의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 문맥상 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 민지는 Jane Goodall을 직접 만난 적이 있다.
민지는 Jane Goodall과 같은 책을 썼다.
민지는 Jane Goodall처럼 되고 싶어 한다.
민지는 Jane Goodall의 침팬지를 돌보고 있다.
민지는 Jane Goodall의 책을 좋아하지 않는다.
items.explain: role model: 본받고 싶은 사람. 뒤에 Like Jane Goodall, I ~ 로 이어진다.

items.stem: 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.box:
G: I'm looking for my cat, Bori. She is missing.
B: Oh, ______________ What does she look like?
G: She has short and gray fur. She has blue eyes.
B: I'll help you. Let's look for your cat together.
G: Thanks!
choices: I hope your dream comes true.
items.explain: 고양이를 잃어버렸다는 말에 대한 유감 표현.

items.stem: 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 적절하게 짝 지어진 것은?
items.box: Ms. Jones was a wise old lady ____ⓐ____ lived next door. Everyone in town came to her when they were in trouble. Later, Carol said, "I saw Tom ____ⓑ____ out of the kitchen."
items.explain: 선행사가 사람(lady) → who. 지각동사 saw + 목적어 + 동사원형/현재분사 → coming.

items.stem: 글을 쓴 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.box: Do you have a problem? Did you lose your bag? I'm sorry to hear that, but don't worry. Just contact Ms. Jones. She has solved a lot of problems. She's good at listening to details. Her phone number is 123-456-7890. You can contact her anytime. Good luck!
choices: To advertise Ms. Jones's help for people in trouble
To report a lost bag to the police
To explain how to find lost items by yourself
To invite neighbors to Ms. Jones's party
To warn people about a thief in town
items.explain: 문제가 있으면 Jones 씨에게 연락하라는 홍보 글.

items.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.box: Hi, my name is Ruby. I want to talk about my grandfather. He is so _____ that he always has good advice. When I made some mistakes on a test, he told me to learn from the mistakes. After that, I didn't make the same mistakes. I'm guided by his wisdom.
items.explain: 항상 좋은 조언을 해 주고, 뒤에 his wisdom 이 나온다 → wise.

items.stem: 글의 흐름으로 보아 <u>어색한</u> 곳은?
items.box: Mom called Ms. Jones to find the person who ate the cake. ⓐ<u>Ms. Jones was a wise old lady who lived next door.</u> ⓑ<u>Everyone in town came to her when they were in trouble.</u> ⓒ<u>She was good at baking chocolate cakes for her neighbors.</u> ⓓ<u>Ms. Jones came with her sweet smile.</u> ⓔ<u>"Don't worry! Let's find out the big eater!"</u>
items.explain: 문제 해결사 Jones 씨를 소개하는 흐름에서 케이크를 잘 굽는다는 말은 어색하다.

items.stem: 우리말 뜻과 일치하도록 주어진 단어를 바르게 배열할 때 <u>네 번째</u>에 오는 단어는?
items.box:
나는 그가 열심히 공부하는 것을 보았다.
( study, him, hard, I, saw )
items.explain: I saw him study hard. → 네 번째 단어는 hard.

items.stem: 다음 중 어법상 옳지 <u>않은</u> 것은?
choices: The room was filled with many books.
I heard someone knock on the door.
She was so tired that she fell asleep right away.
The girl who lost the game look so sad.
The boy whom I met yesterday is my cousin.
items.explain: 주격 관계대명사절의 동사는 선행사에 일치시키고, 문장의 동사는 주어 The girl 에 맞춘다 → looks. ⑤는 목적격 관계대명사 whom 이 바르게 쓰였다.
items.source: 학습지 문법(관계대명사·지각동사·so ~ that·수동태) + 목적격 관계대명사 확장

items.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 수 <u>없는</u> 말을 모두 고른 것은?
items.box: I _____ the dog running in the park.
items.explain: 목적격 보어로 현재분사를 취하는 것은 지각동사(saw, heard, watched). want·tell 은 목적어 + to부정사.

items.stem: 빈칸 어디에도 들어갈 수 <u>없는</u> 단어는? (대소문자 구별하지 않음)
items.box: Her first stop was a room that looked like an old airplane _____. Model airplanes were _____ from the ceiling. A leather pilot jacket and goggles were displayed. When Emily put them on, she could hear the sounds of airplane engines. She looked _____ the room in surprise. On the wall, there was a picture of a woman. She looked brave and strong. Her name was Kwon Ki-ok. She was the first _____ pilot in Korea.
items.explain: garage / hanging / around / female. invited 는 들어갈 곳이 없다.

items.box: Next, Ms. Jones talked to Carol, the daughter. She stayed home all morning. Ms. Jones asked, "What were you doing between 11 and 12?" "I was reading a detective novel in the living room. I went to the kitchen to drink some water and found the box on the table. But I couldn't see the cake inside the box. You know, ⓐ<u>I'm trying to lose weight these days.</u> So, I don't eat any ____ⓑ____. Most of all, I don't like chocolate cake. Too much sugar and butter in it." "When did you go to the kitchen?" "I don't know the exact time, but I saw Tom coming out of the kitchen."

items.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: I'm trying to become thinner these days.
I'm trying to eat more these days.
I'm trying to grow taller these days.
I'm trying to lift heavy things these days.
I'm trying to sleep more these days.
items.explain: lose weight: 살을 빼다.

items.stem: 윗글의 빈칸 ⓑ에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.explain: 살을 빼는 중이라 디저트를 먹지 않는다. 바로 뒤에 초콜릿 케이크 이야기가 이어진다.

items.box: Emily stepped into the next room. The room was filled with many books and drawings of insects and plants. It looked like a small forest. When she closed the door, drawings on the desk suddenly started to fly around the room. She caught one of them. It was a drawing of a honeybee. It was so ____ⓐ____ that the honeybee looked alive. From one of the bookshelves, Emily found a shining book. She picked it up. She saw the name Jean-Henri Fabre on its cover.

items.stem: 윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
items.explain: 너무 자세해서(detailed) 살아 있는 것처럼 보였다.

items.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 방은 모형 비행기로 가득 차 있었다.
Emily가 문을 열자 그림들이 날아다니기 시작했다.
Emily는 책상 위에서 빛나는 책을 발견했다.
책 표지에는 Charles Darwin의 이름이 있었다.
items.explain: It was a drawing of a honeybee. (책·그림으로 가득 / 문을 닫았을 때 / 책장에서 / Fabre)

items.stem: (A)~(D)에 대해 바르게 설명한 사람만을 <보기>에서 <u>모두</u> 고른 것은?
items.box:
Mother Teresa was so caring (A)<u>that</u> she helped many people in India. Mina's uncle is a police officer (B)<u>who</u> always tries to help people in need. Antoni Gaudi was so (C)<u>creative</u> that he made beautiful buildings. Everyone (D)<u>admire</u> these people who make a difference.

<보기>
ⓐ 수연 : (A)의 that은 '너무 ~해서 …하다'라는 뜻의 so ~ that 구문에 쓰인 것으로, 뒤에 「주어+동사」가 온 것이 맞아.
ⓑ 예지 : (B)의 who는 앞의 a police officer를 꾸며 주는 주격 관계대명사니까 that으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어.
ⓒ 민수 : (C)는 so 뒤에 부사가 와야 하니까 creative를 creatively로 고쳐야 해.
ⓓ 지현 : (D)는 주어 Everyone이 단수 취급이라서 admire를 admires로 고쳐야 해.
items.explain: so + 형용사/부사 + that: was 뒤 보어 자리이므로 형용사 creative 가 맞다(ⓒ 틀림). Everyone 은 단수 취급(ⓓ 맞음).
items.source: L6 Express Our Thoughts (Create) · so ~ that · 관계대명사
